user.title: Add a Zendure set
user.description: ZEPHYR reads the set over the local network. Nothing is written to the set in this version.

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the Zendure set. HEMS must be off in the Zendure app.

discovery_confirm.title: Zendure set found
discovery_confirm.description: {model} with {packs} packs ({capacity} kWh), serial number {serial}, at {host}. Add it to ZEPHYR?

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the set or its answer is not usable. Check the address; if it still fails, turn HEMS on once in the Zendure app, leave the menu and turn it off again.

abort.already_configured: This set is already part of ZEPHYR.
abort.set_added: Set {number} has been added to ZEPHYR.
abort.cannot_connect: The set could not be reached.

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the Zendure set. HEMS must be off in the Zendure app.

reconfigure.title: Capacity of the set
reconfigure.description: ZEPHYR recognises most Zendure batteries by itself. Only enter the total capacity of this set when a pack is not recognised. 0 = automatic.

data_description.capacity_override: Total capacity of all batteries of this set together, in kWh. 0 = automatic from the pack table.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the set or its answer is not usable. Check the address; if it still fails, turn HEMS on once in the Zendure app, leave the menu and turn it off again.

abort.already_configured: This set is already part of ZEPHYR.

serial_mismatch.title: Different set at the address of set {number}
serial_mismatch.description: The device at {host} reports a different serial number than set {number}. ZEPHYR does not use it. Check the IP address of the set (for example a fixed address in your router), or remove set {number} and add it again.

unknown_pack.title: Battery of set {number} not recognised
unknown_pack.description: ZEPHYR does not recognise these batteries: {packs}. The capacity of set {number} is therefore too low. Enter the total capacity via ZEPHYR → Set {number} → Reconfigure. Want to help? Report the model and the line above in a GitHub issue, and we will add the battery.

p1_missing.title: No P1 meter chosen
p1_missing.description: ZEPHYR needs your smart meter to calculate. Open Settings → Devices & services → ZEPHYR → Configure and choose the P1 sensor (or the import and export sensors).

live_off_after_restart.title: ZEPHYR no longer controls the battery
live_off_after_restart.description: After a restart live control is off (option "Live control off after a restart"). The set keeps its last power until your current control or you take over. Switch "ZEPHYR controls the battery" on again, or let your current control take over.

second_controller.title: Another system controls the battery
second_controller.description: The set twice reported limits within 5 minutes that ZEPHYR did not write. ZEPHYR stopped writing and is back in shadow mode. Switch off your old control (Gielz, automations, the Zendure app) and then switch "ZEPHYR controls the battery" on again.

price_format.title: Prices of {entity} cannot be read
price_format.description: The price sensor {entity} has a value, but ZEPHYR finds no prices per time slot in its attributes (raw_today / raw_tomorrow with start, end and value). The planner uses zero on the meter until it can read prices. Choose a Nord Pool sensor in the ZEPHYR options, or report the format in an issue on GitHub.

init.title: Sources and battery
init.description: Choose your smart meter (P1) in W: one net sensor (+ when drawing from the grid), or two sensors for import and export (as the DSMR integration provides). ZEPHYR runs in shadow mode: it calculates what it would do, but does not control the battery yet.

data.excluded_hvac_modes: Air conditioner: not from the battery when
data.live_off_after_restart: Live control off after a restart (test phase)
data.expensive_hours: Deliver in the most expensive hours
data.plan_allow_export: Planner: allow export from the battery
data.curtail_negative: Surplus solar at a negative price

data_description.p1_entity: A meter that reports every second controls best. With corrections (EV, air conditioning) you can choose the corrected sensor of your current setup.
data_description.min_soc: Below this value ZEPHYR stops delivering. Written to the set once ZEPHYR controls it.
data_description.max_soc: Above this value ZEPHYR stops charging. Written to the set once ZEPHYR controls it.
data_description.p1_source: Two sensors see every meter telegram, also when the value stays the same. Better than a combined template sensor, which only reports changes.
data_description.p1_import_entity: Power drawn from the grid, for example …_power_consumption.
data_description.p1_export_entity: Power returned to the grid, for example …_power_production.
data_description.solar_forecast_entity: Optional. A forecast sensor with half-hour detail (Solcast: …_forecast_tomorrow). ZEPHYR stores tomorrow's forecast every evening at 23:00, as a yardstick for the planner later.
data_description.solar_energy_entity: Optional. Total solar production in kWh (for example the inverter's energy counter). Read every hour to compare with the forecast.
data_description.solar_power_entities: Optional. Power (W) of inverters that are not on a Zendure set, for example SolarEdge. Several are added up. Not the PV of the Zendure set itself: ZEPHYR already reads that from the set. Without a sensor ZEPHYR estimates the power from the solar energy counter.
data_description.excluded_energy_entity: Optional. Energy counter (kWh) of a load the battery may not feed, such as the air conditioner. ZEPHYR estimates its power from the counter and does not deliver for it; the house's other use still comes from the battery and solar surplus still charges it.
data_description.excluded_climate_entity: Optional. The climate entity of that air conditioner: it tells at once whether it runs and in which mode. Without it, the load is never fed from the battery.
data_description.excluded_hvac_modes: Modes in which the air conditioner may not be fed from the battery. Default: heating.
data_description.live_off_after_restart: After a restart of Home Assistant or a reload, "ZEPHYR controls the battery" is off and you switch it on yourself. Keep this on during the test week.
data_description.price_entity: Optional. With a Nord Pool sensor (today's prices in its attributes) zero-meter control delivers only in the most expensive hours of the day. Without it ZEPHYR delivers whenever the house asks.
data_description.expensive_hours: Hours per day in which ZEPHYR may deliver: the most expensive according to Nord Pool.
data_description.reserve_soc: Extra charge that may be used freely: below it ZEPHYR charges in the cheapest hours before the next expensive block. In the expensive hours it delivers down to the minimum SOC. 0 = off.
data_description.min_price: Optional, bare Nord Pool price: never deliver below it, not even in the most expensive hours.
data_description.tariff_energy_tax: Cost log: per kWh, Netherlands 2026 €0.09161. The all-in price is (market + margin + energy tax) × (1 + VAT).
data_description.tariff_markup_import: Added to the Nord Pool price for every kWh you draw.
data_description.tariff_markup_export: Added to the Nord Pool price for every kWh you return; negative for a fee. Until 2027 net metering also credits energy tax and VAT on export.
data_description.tariff_fixed_month: Optional: standing charges + grid operator − energy tax reduction. Only shown next to the totals, to compare with your annual bill.
data_description.cost_import_counters: Optional: the meter's kWh counters for import (tariff 1 and 2, summed). Without them ZEPHYR integrates the P1 power.
data_description.cost_export_counters: Optional: the meter's kWh counters for export (tariff 1 and 2).
data_description.tariff_solar_bonus: Optional: extra % on (market + export margin) for export between sunrise and sunset, only when that amount is positive. Zonneplan: 10 %.
data_description.tariff_supplier: Choose your supplier: ZEPHYR then takes the margins, solar bonus, energy tax and VAT from its tariff table (fetched from GitHub once a month). Only suppliers whose amounts a user has checked are listed. With "Own tariffs" the fields below apply; the fixed costs per month apply in both cases.
data_description.plan_wear_cost: Advanced. Cost per kWh delivered by the battery that the planner weighs in its choice (not in the costs), so it does not cycle the battery for a few cents. Default €0.03.
data_description.plan_grid_charge_cost: Advanced. Gain per kWh that charging from the grid must bring before the planner does it (only in its choice, not in the costs), so it does not buy at an expensive moment for a cent. Default €0.01.
data_description.plan_allow_export: The planner may deliver at full power and export the rest when that pays (action Export). Off by default.
data_description.plan_load_margin: The planner chooses as if the house uses this much more (buffer against a low estimate). Not in the costs. 0 = off.
data_description.plan_buffer: The planner never plans below the minimum state of charge plus this buffer; the controller may use it when the house uses more than expected. 0 = off.
data_description.vacation_when_away: Switches the vacation on by itself when nobody has been home (zone.home = 0) for 24 hours, and off when someone is back. While on vacation the planner uses the standby use, the air conditioner counts as off, and the hours are learned apart from the normal profile.
data_description.workday_entity: Optional. The binary sensor of the Workday integration. Holidays then count as weekend days in the consumption profile (learning and planning). Without it: Monday-Friday are workdays.
data_description.curtail_negative: What happens to surplus solar when the export price is below zero. Off: it is exported and costs money, the planner makes room in the battery first. Another system: an inverter limiter curtails it by itself. ZEPHYR: ZEPHYR blocks export of the sets' own panels and turns on the switch below.
data_description.curtail_switch: On while the export price is negative (only with ZEPHYR).
data_description.curtail_number: Number entity that limits the inverter's power in % (e.g. SolarEdge Modbus active power limit). Only with ZEPHYR curtails.
data_description.curtail_inverter_w: Rated AC power of that inverter (W), to turn the wanted production into a %. 0 = not set.

error.p1_pair_incomplete: Choose both the import and the export sensor.
error.p1_pair_same: Import and export must be two different sensors.
error.excluded_needs_counter: An air-conditioner climate entity only works together with its energy counter. Choose the counter or clear the climate entity.

live_not_possible.message: ZEPHYR cannot control the battery now: {reasons}.

test_live.message: The write test only works in shadow mode ("ZEPHYR controls the battery" off).

test_not_standby.message: Set ZEPHYR to the mode Standby first for the write test.

export_period.message: The start date must not be after the end date.

no_planner.message: The planner is not running (choose a price sensor in the options).

test_command.name: Write test
test_command.description: Sends one fixed command to the set(s) and puts them back in standby after the chosen duration. Only in shadow mode with the mode Standby.

export_costs.name: Export costs
export_costs.description: Writes every stored quarter of the period (costs, energy, prices) as CSV to config/zephyr/. Without dates: this month.

start.name: Start
start.description: First day (default: the first of the month of the end date).

recalculate.name: Recalculate plan
recalculate.description: Makes a new plan now (otherwise the planner calculates every quarter and on new prices).

reset_profile.name: Reset consumption profile
reset_profile.description: Forgets the learned consumption per hour. By default it is filled again from the recorder (meter counters, last 28 days).

refill.name: Fill again
refill.description: Fill the profile again from the recorder. Off: start empty and learn from the coming hours.

get_plan.name: Get plan
get_plan.description: Returns the current plan: state, figures, blocks and the quarters with action, prices, solar, consumption and expected state of charge.
